mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 60 days, investors anticipate continued easing, which lowers real discount rates and boosts equity present-value pricing, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.5% for 60 consecutive days (below 5-year monthly average)
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 1-month prior period (t-test p > 0.05), or the 5-year average FEDFUNDS rate is not meaningfully lower than the pre-window average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp, one-time increase in the CPIAUCSL above 0.3% in a month signals accelerating inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to raise rates, which compresses equity discounting and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar inflation surprise events, or the 5-day moving average of 10-y TIPS yields does not rise after the CPIAUCSL spike.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 for three consecutive months indicates labor market strengthening, which reduces recession risk and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 100 such labor-cycle events, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the 3-month moving average of UNRATE does not decline during the period.

mechanism_narrative: When the RSAFS (retail sales) unexpectedly exceeds the prior month by more than 10% and persists for two months, it signals robust consumer demand, prompting higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >10% in month t and again in month t+1
failure_condition: In 10 such demand events, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the 3-month moving average of HOUST does not rise during the event window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 2% in a month followed by a sustained decline of 4% over the next two months predicts supply-side weakness, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >2% in month t, then declines >4% cumulatively over next two months
failure_condition: Over 8 such episodes, SPX 60-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05), or the 12-month moving average of GDP growth is not materially lower than the pre-shock trend.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both move in the same direction (both up or both down) for at least 10 consecutive months, it indicates a coordinated policy and labor market response, reinforcing expectations of stable policy rates and supporting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE show parallel direction for ≥10 consecutive months
regime_hint: coordinated policy and labor market alignment
failure_condition: In 20 such interaction events, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and UNRATE exceeds 0.9 during the event window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% for two consecutive months in a context of rising CPIAUCSL suggests a shift toward tighter labor market conditions, which can erode equity risk premia and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for 2 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL increases in the same months
regime_hint: labor market tightening with inflationary pressures
failure_condition: Over 12 such episodes, SPX 5-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05), or the 3-month moving average of HOUST does not decline during the episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the 5-week moving average of GDPC1 (GDP personal consumption expenditures) grows at a rate exceeding 3% above the 12-month prior average for two consecutive quarters, it signals robust economic momentum that supports higher corporate profits and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: 5-week GDPC1 MA growth > 3% above 12-month prior MA for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: In 15 such acceleration events, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the 4-quarter moving average of industrial production does not also exceed its prior average during the event window.
